intent: Dates that mean something: typed entries, lead days, and the one module both arms consume.
change: Calendar entry semantics in packages/engine: deadline and subscription_renewal types, per-entry reminder lead days, auto-cancel flag and lead threshold, due-computation over entries, send/enqueue idempotence keys, and the entry annotation states (handled, declined, needs-attention, late).
done_when: Unit tests prove due computation across types, lead days, and boundary dates; integration tests prove annotation transitions persist on the s1 schema and idempotence keys are unique per (entry, day) and (entry, renewal).

proofs.claim: Before the calendar ledger exists, the suite that marks an entry, records one reminder per (entry, day) and one auto-cancel per (entry, renewal) on the migrated schema cannot load: it fails at import because the db calendar-ledger module is not there.

On the s1 schema plus migration 0007, an entry carries its lead days, auto-cancel flag and threshold with defaults; a mark on an entry persists with note and time and only a mark of equal or higher rank may replace it; recordReminder is one row per (entry, day) and recordAutoCancel one per (entry, renewal), returning the existing row on a repeat, with the database itself refusing a duplicate; the records go with the entry; and the migration set still creates exactly the declared tables and re-applies as a no-op.

Due computation is right across both kinds, lead days, and boundary dates: a reminder is owed from the lead day to the date and late after the first day, an auto-cancel from its own threshold to the renewal and never for a deadline, a done, handled, undated or unflagged entry; date arithmetic crosses months, years and leap days on the string and reads the day off the person’s clock; annotation ranks refuse a weaker mark over a stronger one; the dispatch vocabularies and keys are what the scan will write; the schema declares the new tables, cascades and unique keys and the package exports them.
Lint, typecheck (build and test configs), the full suite with coverage thresholds (100% on core), and both builds pass with the calendar semantics in place.

intent: The daily heartbeat: every dated entry becomes exactly one timely Telegram nudge.
change: pg-boss cron scan job computing due reminders and dispatching through s3's sendToUser with record-before-dispatch idempotence, delivered/failed/skipped-unbound/late states, bounded retry on next scan, and late-send for missed windows.
done_when: Integration tests with a scripted send sink prove exactly-once under re-run and crash-between-record-and-dispatch, unbound-user skip, failed-send retry on next scan, late-marked sends after a downtime window, and pickup of chat-created entries.

proofs.claim: Before the scan, the worker outbound door and the adapter exist, the composed reminder path (chat tool entry -> pg-boss scan -> bot outbound over the test transport) fails.

The composed reminder path delivers once through the real outbound door and records delivery, failure and unbound skip; the scan module proves exactly-once under re-run, overlap and crash, bounded retry, late sends with the entry marked, per-person clocks, and the cron registration.
The reminder wording, the per-zone clock, and the outbound-door adapter hold as pure units, and the core index still exports every calendar vocabulary.
The repository gate (lint, typecheck, tests with coverage, build) passes with the scan, the adapter and the worker composition in place.

intent: The renewal date that pulls a trigger - but only a human can release the safety.
change: The scan's auto-cancel arm enqueuing an s5 cancellation task once per renewal date, the leading Telegram confirm question via the UserIO gate, promotion of s3 pending-question routing to the production UserIO implementation (scripted double retained for tests), and entry annotation on every ending.
done_when: Integration tests on fixtures via LocalProvider with scripted UserIO prove confirm-yes through to a cancelled fixture member with event trail, decline and timeout leaving membership untouched and the entry annotated, unlinked-entry needs-attention with the reminder still sent, and enqueue idempotence under re-run.

proofs.claim: Before the planner, the confirm gate and the scan arm exist, the composed auto-cancel path (entry at lead day -> scan enqueues -> confirm question -> fakegym playbook on LocalProvider) fails.

On fixtures with a scripted person: one confirm-gated task per renewal under concurrent scans, yes runs the fakegym playbook to a cancelled member and a handled entry, no and silence leave the membership untouched and mark the entry, an unlinked entry is marked for attention with its reminder still sent, and a failed playbook leaves the entry marked and re-armed for the next renewal; the bot carries a chat reply to the task ledger as an answer or a decline through the production sink.
The consent vocabulary, the confirm question wording, the action-to-site reading, the extended auto-cancel states, the confirm gate over a mission, and the Telegram UserIO adapter hold as pure units.
The repository gate (lint, typecheck, tests with coverage, build) passes with the auto-cancel arm, the confirm gate, the bot sink promotion and the worker composition in place.

intent: The proof no fixture can fake: a real phone buzzes, a real yes, the task finishes.
change: The live proof workflow gated on TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN: a real reminder delivered to the bound account, and the full auto-cancel round-trip - real confirm question in Telegram, real answer, task resumes and completes against the fixture - with skip-with-reason when the token is absent and the run recorded.
done_when: The gated live suite delivers a real reminder and completes the confirm round-trip against the fixture with the task succeeded and events recorded; without the token the suite skips with an explicit reason; the run procedure is documented in the repo.

proofs.claim: Before the bot exports the live gate, the live round-trip suite - the composed path of real bot, real ask, real answer, task resumes - cannot even decide whether to run.
Without the opt-in, the token or the chat, the live suite skips with the reason in its name and the run exits zero; the reminder path still holds with the arm counts on the scan report.

The live gate opens only with the flag, the token and a numeric chat id; .env.example documents both halves of the opt-in blank and the gate reads it as shut; the README names only scripts and files that exist.

With the owner token and phone: a real reminder is delivered to the bound chat, the confirm question and the gym code question are answered from the phone, the task succeeds against the fakegym fixture and the entry is marked handled.
The repository gate (lint, typecheck, tests with coverage, build) passes with the live suite, the gate module, the bot process and the documentation in place.

intent: What the scan writes on an entry is worth nothing until the person can read it.
change: The dashboard calendar entry shows the mark an engine left on it and the note beside it, each mark in the reader's words (late reminder, needs attention, auto-cancel declined, cancelled); the web client's CalendarItem carries the annotation columns GET /calendar-items already returns; the view-model carries them into the row; the page prints them.
done_when: The view-model unit suite proves each mark is worded with its note and an unmarked entry shows nothing; the calendar page browser proof shows a seeded needs_attention entry with its note on the page and an unmarked entry without.

proofs.claim: Before the view-model carries the mark, the unit suite asserting each mark is worded with its note fails.

expected.failure_signature: carries the mark an engine left on an entry

proofs.claim: The view-model words every mark with its note and leaves an unmarked entry bare, and the calendar page shows a seeded needs_attention entry with its note and an unmarked entry without.
Lint, typecheck, tests with coverage thresholds and both builds pass on the whole tree.

intent: A person nobody can reach is told so on the entry, not lost in a table nobody reads.
change: The scan marks an entry needs_attention with a dated note when its reminder is skipped for want of a bound Telegram chat, so the recorded skip the reminder-path spec promises is on the dashboard entry; the auto-cancel arm records unlinked with the same reason for a flagged renewal whose person has no bound chat, instead of arming a task whose question nobody can receive and that times out a day later marked as unanswered.
done_when: The scan integration suite proves an unbound skip leaves the mark and dated note on the entry once and never over a stronger mark, and that a flagged renewal for an unbound person is recorded unlinked with no task and the reason on the entry; the auto-cancel suite proves the same through the worker composition; the root reminders suite proves the mark on an entry created through the API.

proofs.claim: Before the scan marks the entry, the scan suite asserting the unbound skip and the unbound auto-cancel land on the entry fails.

expected.failure_signature: records a flagged renewal as unlinked for a person with no chat to ask over

proofs.claim: An unbound skip marks the entry needs_attention with the dated note once and never over a stronger mark; a flagged renewal for an unbound person is recorded unlinked with no task and the reason on the entry, through the scan alone and through the worker composition; the mark reaches the API the dashboard reads.
Lint, typecheck, tests with coverage thresholds and both builds pass on the whole tree.
